faqs.a:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning:
Apiary
means a place where bee colonies are kept.
Bee
means any stage of the common domestic honeybee, Apis Mellifera species. Bee does
               not include any type of non-domestic bee.
Beekeeper
means any person who is in possession of, or who is keeping, harboring, or caring
               for any bee hive box or colony, or any person 18 years of age or older who has right
               of property in any bee hive box or colony, or any person who allows a bee hive box
               or colony on his or her property. The parent, guardian, or legal custodian of any
               child under the age of 18 who owns, keeps, harbors, or cares for any bee hive box
               or colony shall be deemed to be the beekeeper.
Bottom board
means a long flat panel, typically made of wood or plastic, that is placed beneath
               a hive box but atop a hive box stand or other foundation structure that together,
               serve to elevate and protect the colony.
Brood
means any eggs, larvae, and pupae that will become bees.
Brood comb
means a hive box frame that consists mainly of brood.
Colony
means a hive box stand or foundation structure, a bottom board, a hive box or boxes,
               a queen excluder, a super or supers, an inner cover, and a top or outer cover all
               stacked atop each other, and appurtences attached thereto, including bees, comb, honey,
               pollen, and brood. It also means any group of bees residing within, or outside of,
               a hive box.
Frame
means a structural element fitting into a hive box that is typically made of wood
               or plastic, and that holds or provides support for a honeycomb or brood comb.
Hive box
means a box-like structure, typically made of wood or plastic, intended for the housing
               of a bee colony. A hive box is sometimes known as a hive body or brood chamber. Hive
               boxes includes observation hives.
Honeycomb
is a beeswax structure of hexagonal cells made by bees and used to hold larvae and
               store honey.
Nucleus colony
means a structure, usually composed of a brood frame or frames and attached bees,
               and that is used to create a new colony.
Observation hive
means a special purpose hive box structure that is no wider than a single frame,
               but that may be longer and taller than a single frame, that has glass or transparent
               sides to facilitate the viewing of activity inside the observation hive, and that
               has an attached tube-shaped device that allows for direct movement of bees from the
               observation hive to the outdoors. Observation hives are normally placed in or near
               a window and are typically used for educational or recreational viewing purposes.
Queen excluder
means a frame that encloses a metal or screened panel that is placed between the
               uppermost hive box and the lowest super and that serves to keep the queen out of the
               super.
Super
means a box-like structure, typically placed atop a hive box or queen excluder but
               beneath a top cover, that is used to store honey, and that allows a beekeeper to extract
               surplus honey without harm to the colony.
Top cover
means a lid that is typically made of wood or plastic, and that is placed on top
               of a hive box or super to protect the colony.
Tract
means a contiguous parcel of land under common ownership.
(
Ord. No. 4345, § 1, 8-6-2012
)
